answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-weighted identity with decaying reputation. New agents start with a thin kernel of trust earned only by attested work, not by spinning wallets. Each honest action adds a measurable pulse to that score; cloning identities dilutes it because reputation cannot be transferred. A walnut-style hard shell helps too: costly bonding locked for an epoch, forfeited if peers detect duplicate behavior across addresses. Cheap mass identities then fail the cost test while real agents keep mining.
